subject: panel of geom_tile does not appear

messages.author: cb1a292793a52332
messages.subject: panel of geom_tile does not appear
parts:
Hi all,

I've been running into some troubles with ggplot2

I have a data frame with 9*400 observations for ~30 variables, that I represent using a geom_tile

My problem is that the last combination of factors is not plotted in the figure, despite being perfectly OK (and it appears when I used lattice)

See below for one of the resulting graphs (and some code)

If any one has an idea, that would be really great

t



My call is

base <- ggplot(ep,aes(x=rhoi,y=rhor)) + facet_grid(ri~Ur) +
scale_y_log10() +
scale_x_log10() +
scale_fill_gradientn(colours=pal) +
xlab('Resource input') +
ylab('Resource mortality') + theme_bw()
print(base + geom_tile(aes(fill=vEve)))

with 

> dim(ep)
[1] 3661   75

Just to make sure that all the combinations do indeed have data in them

> lapply(split(ep,list(ep$ri,ep$Ur)),dim)
$`R: 1.Frequency: 0.05`
[1] 607  75

$`R: 10.Frequency: 0.05`
[1] 613  75

$`R: 1.Frequency: 0.4`
[1] 610  75

$`R: 10.Frequency: 0.4`
[1] 609  75

$`R: 1.Frequency: 0.75`
[1] 611  75

$`R: 10.Frequency: 0.75`
[1] 611  75

messages.subject: Re: panel of geom_tile does not appear
parts:
Timothee

It is rather difficult to guess what is going on without knowing
something about your data.

Is it possible to create a reduced dataset that demonstrates the
problem? You could, for example, create a dummy dataset using random
values, e.g:

ep <- data.frame(
rhoi=runif(100, 0, 10),
rhor=runif(100, 0, 10),
ri=rdiscrete(100, 4),
Ur=rdiscrete(100, 4),
pal=rnorm(100),
vEve=rdiscrete(100, 5))

Alternatively, could you create a subset of your data.frame and use
dput() to capture the values and post the results here?

Andrie
